Sugar @ nucleum fragment modifier marks a fragment-shader entry on the nucleum surface.

Syntax: @ nucleum fragment

Category#

lane

Related#

  • nucleum
  • annotation-sugar

Examples#

radix/corpus/annotation-sugar/nucleum-fragment.fab (canonical · annotation)#

Sugar @ nucleum fragment modifier marks a fragment-shader entry on the nucleum surface.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — sugar @ nucleum fragment modifier
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Sugar modifier — `@ nucleum fragment` on a function declaration marks
#     it as the fragment-shader entry (NucleumRole::Fragment); the parser
#     reads `fragment` as structured modifier data on the nucleum annotation,
#     never as an untyped name/argument pair
#   • The la reader spelling — `nucleum` is the la surface of the kernel
#     annotation identity; the en twin is `@ kernel fragment`
#   • A marked fragment function is a systems/shaders entry, not a host
#     entry — the plain `incipit` driver below proves the module still
#     checks and runs on the host lane
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • writing `@ fragment` alone — the bare fragment name stays the graphics
#     statement annotation, not the nucleum modifier
#   • expecting the marked function to be called from a host `incipit`
#
# See also: nucleum, annotation-sugar
# =============================================================================

@ nucleum { fragment = verum }
functio umbra() → vacuum {
}

functio identitas(numerus x) → numerus {
    redde x
}

incipit {
    nota identitas(5)
}

Expected output:

5

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/argument-escape.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot be passed to an ordinary function argument.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject ordinary-argument escape
# =============================================================================

fn apply(int value) → int {
    return value
}

fn take() → void {
    const _ kernel ← (int value) kernel ∴ value
    const int result ← apply(kernel)
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/bag-result.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot return a host list/bag, including an append-built result.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject list/bag result protocol
# =============================================================================
# A list is a host-managed bag/result carrier. The closure cannot return it,
# even when it is populated with append before the return.
# =============================================================================

fn take(int value) → void {
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel → list<int> ∴ do {
        var list<int> items ← empty
        items.append(value)
        return items
    }
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/bare-body.fab (supporting · reject)#

A compact closure body cannot be a bare block; use do in the body joint.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject bare compact brace body
# =============================================================================

main {
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel ∴ {
        return value
    }
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/cape.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot contain do/catch recovery.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject cape/catch recovery in closure body
# =============================================================================

fn take(int value) → void {
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel → int ∴ do {
        do {
            const int probe ← value
        } catch err {
            print err
        }
        return value
    }
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/capture.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot capture an enclosing value local.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject enclosing local capture
# =============================================================================

main {
    const int seed ← 2
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel ∴ value + seed
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/dynamic-value.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot produce a nested dynamic closure value.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject dynamic closure value
# =============================================================================

fn take(int value) → void {
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel ∴ (int inner) ∴ inner
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/error-channel.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot declare an alternate-exit error channel.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject closure error channel
# =============================================================================

main {
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel → int ⇥ string ∴ value
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/field-escape.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot be stored in a field.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject field escape
# =============================================================================

class Capsule {
    int stored
}

fn take() → void {
    const _ kernel ← (int value) kernel ∴ value
    const Capsule boxed ← Capsule { stored = kernel }
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/host-effect.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot perform host output.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject host effect in closure body
# =============================================================================

fn take(int value) → void {
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel → int ∴ do {
        print value
        return value
    }
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/list-escape.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot be stored in a list.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject list escape
# =============================================================================

fn take() → void {
    const _ kernel ← (int value) kernel ∴ value
    const list<int> items ← [kernel, kernel]
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/reject.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot use a reject guard that throws.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject reject guard in closure body
# =============================================================================

fn take(int value) → void {
    const _ bad ← (int value) kernel → int ∴ do {
        reject value > 10 throw value
        return value
    }
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/return-escape.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot be returned as an outer function value.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject return escape
# =============================================================================

fn take() → void {
    const _ kernel ← (int value) kernel ∴ value
    return kernel
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/source-callback.fab (supporting · reject)#

A kernel closure cannot capture a host source callback value.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject source callback capture
# =============================================================================
# A source callback is an enclosing function value. Referencing it from a
# kernel closure is a capture and therefore cannot cross the device boundary.
# =============================================================================

fn take((string, int) → int source, int value) → void {
    const _ bad ← (int x) kernel → int ∴ source("weights", x)
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/stack-free-kernel.fab (supporting · reject)#

A closure cannot stack free and kernel modifiers.

# =============================================================================
# nucleum — reject stacked free then kernel modifiers
# =============================================================================

main {
    const _ bad ← (int value) free kernel ∴ value
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/kernel-closure/stack-kernel-free.fab (supporting · reject)#

A closure cannot stack kernel and free modifiers.
